implementationRisks.title: Existing protected course reads do not implement persisted course membership and institute authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: After authentication, the handler queries syllabus items and the actor's submissions by caller-selected courseId without first proving approved enrollment, instructor assignment, Admin authority, or institute equality.

The handler reads gradeable items and private feedback using courseId and actor ID but never verifies that the actor is a STUDENT with APPROVED enrollment in that course or that the course belongs to the actor's institute.
Any authenticated session can retrieve instructor and approved-student identity data for an arbitrary existing courseId; no COURSE_READ relationship or institute constraint is present.
Any authenticated session can select an arbitrary course and receive course, instructor, institute, syllabus, and announcement data without the designed COURSE_READ predicate.
Announcements and broadcasts are queried directly by courseId before any enrollment, assignment, Admin, or institute authorization.

implementationRisks.impact: Until implemented, authenticated users, including SUPER_USER, unknown roles, and unrelated normal users, can obtain protected data from courses with which they have no persisted relationship.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Implement the revised COURSE_READ or STUDENT_WORK predicate before each protected query, using the canonical actor and a course lookup constrained by actual institute and enrollment/assignment/Admin authority. Return 403 for denied roles and a uniform safe 404 for absent or foreign resources, and prevent shared caching of identity-scoped responses.

implementationRisks.title: Existing teaching boundaries do not fully implement canonical aliases, institute binding, and relationship-first authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: The role check omits canonical INSTRUCTOR and the course lookup does not select or constrain instituteId; authorization therefore does not implement the full TEACH contract.
The role check omits INSTRUCTOR and the course lookup verifies ownership but not the instructor's actual home institute or course institute.
GET omits INSTRUCTOR and authorizes from a course record that lacks institute binding; PATCH repeats the same pattern at lines 93-109.
The handler omits INSTRUCTOR and checks only role plus instructorId, without constraining the course to its actual institute.

The handler parses protected content and creates an announcement for caller-selected courseId for any authenticated actor, with no TEACH role, assignment, institute, or course-existence authorization.

implementationRisks.impact: Until remediation, legitimate INSTRUCTOR aliases regress on several routes, while the stream mutation permits unauthorized course writes; incomplete institute checks also leave cross-institute inconsistencies in teaching operations.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Use one canonical role resolver with PROFESSOR/TEACHER/INSTRUCTOR aliases and UNKNOWN fail-closed. Resolve courseId through a TEACH query that binds instructor assignment and institute, with Admin's specified system scope, before body parsing or effects. Apply the same parent authorization to enrollment, notification, attachment, and announcement effects.

implementationRisks.title: Gradebook export currently delegates with no persisted course authorization

sourceEvidence.explanation: The route checks only PROFESSOR or ADMIN and passes caller-selected courseId to exportGradebookSkill; it omits TEACH assignment and institute validation and excludes TEACHER/INSTRUCTOR aliases.

implementationRisks.impact: A professor may request an unrelated course's exported roster and grade data if the delegated skill lacks an independent guard, while legitimate instructor aliases are rejected.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Implement the design's independently guarded exportGradebookSkill: reauthenticate the canonical actor and constrain the course to instructor assignment plus matching institute, or Admin authority, before any roster/grade queries or CSV construction. The route should preserve the same fail-closed boundary.

implementationRisks.title: CodeLab tutor has not implemented the revised EXEC role and persisted-template boundary

sourceEvidence.explanation: The handler authenticates and checks ICS eligibility, but it does not reject SUPER_USER or UNKNOWN explicitly and does not resolve or authorize the supplied templateId through enrollment, instructor assignment, owned attempt, or Admin authority before the outbound harness call.
The current 500 response returns error.message, contrary to the revised requirement that protected failures not disclose raw exception details.

implementationRisks.impact: Until implementation, unsupported roles may reach the external AI effect, and any future use of templateId risks cross-course context access without its persisted parent authorization. Raw exception messages may disclose internal or rejected data.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Immediately after canonical authentication, require a recognized legacy EXEC role and persisted ICS institute. If templateId affects execution, resolve it through its actual course and enforce enrollment/owned attempt, instructor assignment, or Admin authority before parsing sensitive context or invoking the harness. Return a fixed generic failure body and keep raw details out of client output.

implementationRisks.title: Required production metadata-governance identities and dataset bindings remain unassigned

sourceEvidence.symbol: META-01 exact disclosure and operational contract
sourceEvidence.explanation: The supplied design explicitly states that the trusted academic/privacy approver, manifest maintainer/release reviewer, production dataset ID/fingerprint and attestation procedure, approval lifetime owner, and revocation publication/runbook owner are REQUIRED HUMAN/OPERATOR ASSIGNMENTS and are not supplied.

implementationRisks.impact: A production manifest cannot be trusted, approved, bound to the real dataset, expired, or revoked under accountable governance. The deny-by-default rule therefore blocks all production oversight disclosure until these assignments exist.
implementationRisks.recommendation: Before deployment, institution governance must name the approver and independent maintainer/release reviewer, and operators must define the production dataset fingerprint and attestation, approval lifetime, and versioned publication/revocation runbook. Do not invent identities or admit production metadata while any assignment is absent.

coverage.assessment: Reviewed POST against EXEC: canonical actor, recognized-role denial, persisted ICS, optional template relationship, effect ordering, external harness invocation, and safe failure. Revised design is adequate; current gaps are unimplemented baseline risks.

Reviewed POST against TEACH: instructor aliases, course assignment, institute binding, enrollment-derived recipients, notification side effects, SUPER_USER denial, and pre-parse ordering. Design is adequate; source remains unremediated.

Reviewed GET against COURSE_READ and POST against TEACH, including course-parent authorization, own student submissions, instructor aliases, institute scope, attachments, notifications, and denial ordering. No revised-design defect identified.

Reviewed both methods against TEACH, including course ownership, institute scope, enrollment-to-course binding, target student relevance, mutation/notification ordering, aliases, and safe 404 behavior. Design is adequate but unimplemented.

Reviewed GET and its required direct service boundary against TEACH, including reauthentication, assignment/institute checks before roster/grade reads, aliases, CSV construction, and SUPER_USER denial. No design defect found.

Reviewed GET against TEACH for course assignment, institute binding, roster, syllabus, submission, attachment, and grading-policy reads. Revised policy supplies the necessary parent-bound authorization; implementation is outstanding.

Reviewed GET against STUDENT_WORK, including STUDENT-only role, approved enrollment, actual institute, owned submissions, course-bound private comments, and safe denial. Design is adequate; source lacks these checks.

Reviewed GET against COURSE_READ for constrained membership/assignment/Admin enumeration, institute binding, roster disclosure, SUPER_USER denial, and safe foreign-resource behavior. No design defect identified.

Reviewed GET against COURSE_READ, including persisted course/institute and actor relationship, nested syllabus/announcement reads, response construction, and denial before disclosure. Existing exposure is an implementation risk.

Reviewed GET against COURSE_READ and POST against TEACH, including parent-bound announcement/broadcast reads, role aliases, institute/assignment enforcement, protected body parsing, write ordering, and SUPER_USER denial. Revised design is adequate; current POST is critically under-guarded.

limitations: This was a document-only pre-implementation architecture review using only the supplied sanitized packet; no implementation, runtime, transaction, test, database, build, or deployment evidence was evaluated or claimed.

The body of exportGradebookSkill and notification helpers was not assigned as source in this subset. Their required independent authorization and parent binding were assessed from the revised design contract, while their present implementation state is not asserted beyond the visible route call boundary.

Operational governance identities, production dataset fingerprint, attestation procedure, approval lifetime, and publication/revocation ownership were intentionally not supplied; deny-by-default blocks production disclosure until humans/operators assign them.
